# Attained affine-invariant buffered bad minima

This is a conditional extremal-existence theorem, not the missing sharp
inequality. It combines the original-depth minimal-base compactification
with the new invariant buffered depth. No restriction inequality for the
buffered functional is asserted or used.

## 1. Fixed-base setting and the original minimality hypothesis

Let d>=1, N=d+1, and let P be a nonempty finite lattice-complete base in
its inherited affine lattice. Write m=|P| and k=k(P) for its occupied
parity count. A positive compatible family consists of d-dimensional
convex bodies K_z such that every anchored representation
z=sum lambda_w w implies sum lambda_w K_w subset K_z. Its canonical
hull is conv union_z ({z} times K_z). The measured set consists of the
sampled fibers, with mu=sum_z vol_d and mass M.

The original normalized maximum closed-halfspace depth is beta_0(K).
Set tau=gamma_d/k. Assume the following original-depth minimal-base
properties:

(a) P is dependence-connected and every scalar function preserving
    its anchored convex representations is the restriction of an
    affine function on aff(P).
(b) inf_K beta_0(K)<tau.
(c) Every proper closed subset T=P intersect conv(T), after its
    canonical lift, has original normalized depth at least
    gamma_d/k(T) for every positive compatible family on that lift.

A strict OC counterexample with positive-dimensional fibers supplies
such a base, with k no larger than the original 2^n, by
`candidate 2086e4eaa4bce465`, Sections 5--6,
and `candidate c280bb0dcfd30f3d`, Sections 1--6,
using the parity budget in place of the false arbitrary-base Helly
numerical target. No numerical theorem for arbitrary finite bases is
used here.

Choose a reference family K^ref and b such that

    beta_0(K^ref)<b<tau.                                      (1)

## 2. Compactness of the whole original bad sublevel

Consider all compatible positive families with M=1 and beta_0<=b.
Their fiber masses have a uniform positive lower bound v>0. Otherwise
take a sequence with at least one vanishing mass and pass to limits of
all m masses. Let T be the nonempty set of positive limiting masses.
Compatibility makes T closed: if z is a convex combination of sources
in T, fixing all but one source point gives |K_z|>=lambda^d|K_w| for
some positive lambda and w in T. Hence z also has positive limiting
mass. The retained mass M_T tends to 1.

The ORIGINAL restriction inequality and the fact that canonical lifting
can only decrease original depth give, for every member of the sequence,

    beta_0(full)>=M_T beta_0(restriction)
                >=M_T beta_0(canonical lifted restriction).

By (c), the right side is at least M_T gamma_d/k(T). If T were proper,
letting the sequence tend to its mass limit would give

    b>=gamma_d/k(T)>=gamma_d/k=tau,

contrary to (1). This proves the claimed uniform v without any shape
or position convergence and without a buffered restriction inequality.

The diameter-propagation and representation-matrix lemmas of
`candidate dbf3b23d25004153`, Sections 3--5,
now apply uniformly on this WHOLE sublevel. Normalize one fiber by a
determinant-one continuous linear map. Dependence-connectedness,
volume bounds v<=|K_z|<=1, and the finitely fixed representation
coefficients give a common diameter bound. Project the centroid array
onto the space of representation-preserving arrays. By (a), that
projection is one affine function of the base, so subtracting it is
an actual ambient affine shear. The residual arrays are uniformly
bounded by the representation-matrix singular-value bound. Thus there
is one R such that every family in this sublevel can be mapped into

    M=1,  |K_z|>=v,  K_z subset R B_d for every z.               (2)

All the maps preserve base labels, compatible fibers, closed ambient
halfspaces and normalized original depth. They consist only of a
common continuous linear map, a translation, and an affine continuous
shear depending on the base; each preserves the mixed lattice.

The set A of compatible families satisfying (2) and beta_0<=b is
compact for simultaneous Hausdorff convergence. Bounded convex-set
compactness gives subsequences, volume continuity retains v, all
Minkowski inclusions persist, and original depth is continuous by its
fiberwise slab estimate and total-variation convergence. Every limit
therefore remains positive. The normalization need not be unique or
continuous: only existence of a representative in this one compact
set is used.

## 3. Definition and invariance of the buffered functional

For y in int K define the projective energy

    E_K(y)=min_a integral_K [1+a.(X-y)]^(-N) dX,

where the denominator is strictly positive on K. Extend E by zero at
boundary marks. The energy lemmas already proved in the projective
route give uniqueness of the minimizing parameter, E<=|K|,
joint continuity under positive-body Hausdorff convergence including
boundary marks, and concavity of E^(1/d) on compatible marked fibers.
For boundary continuity one can use E<=N T, where T is the maximal
mass of a submeasure dominated by uniform volume with centroid y;
the hinge formula makes T continuous and zero at boundary marks.

For the actual family put

    Sigma_K=(1/M)sum_z integral_(K_z)
                       (X-g_z)(X-g_z)^T dX,
    G_K(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma_K u),
    f_K(z,y)=(E_(K_z)(y)/M)^(1/N).

Sigma_K is positive definite because each fiber has nonempty interior.
For epsilon>=0 define the raw buffered depth by the infimum of the
following masses:

 * all closed pure-base halfspaces containing z;
 * for a arbitrary and u nonzero, the mass of

       a.(Z-z)+u.(X-y)>=-epsilon f_K(z,y)G_K(u).                (3)

Call it b_epsilon,K(z,y), and let beta_epsilon(K) be its maximum over
actual sampled points divided by M. When epsilon=0 this is precisely
original depth. Halfspace homogeneity permits ||u||=1 for estimates,
or G_K(u)=1 for the source-balance theorem. These are parametrizations
of the same directional infimum.

The maps used in Section 2 preserve beta_epsilon as well. Under
X'=A X+Bz+c, E and M both multiply by |det A|, so f is unchanged;
within-fiber covariance becomes A Sigma A^T, and the continuous
covector becomes A^(-T)u. Thus G is unchanged on transformed covectors.
The affine base-covector correction gives exactly the same inequality
(3) in the transformed coordinates. All normalized captured masses
are unchanged. Base unimodular changes have the same property.

## 4. Continuity, uniformly over all directions

Suppose K_j converges fiberwise in Hausdorff distance to a positive
family K, and actual candidate points y_j in K_(j,p) converge to y in
K_p at one fixed base p. The measures converge in total variation;
write Delta_j=sum_z |K_(j,z) symmetric-difference K_z|, so Delta_j->0.
The masses, covariances and their positive square roots converge.
Joint energy continuity gives f_(K_j)(p,y_j)->f_K(p,y).

Normalize all nonvertical u by ||u||=1. The difference between the
continuous thresholds in (3), at y_j and y, is at most

 eta_j=||y_j-y||+epsilon sup_(||u||=1)
       |f_(K_j)(p,y_j)G_(K_j)(u)-f_K(p,y)G_K(u)| ->0.           (4)

This bound is independent of the possibly unbounded base tilt a.
All old and new fibers lie in a common ball. A slab of width eta_j
in any unit continuous direction has mixed mass at most L eta_j,
where L=m kappa_(d-1) R_1^(d-1) for a common radius R_1 and kappa_0=1.
Consequently every paired nonvertical cap differs in mass by at most
Delta_j+L eta_j. For pure-base caps the difference is at most Delta_j:
the same finite subset of complete fibers is selected, including every
fiber on its CLOSED boundary. Taking infima preserves the uniform
bound. Therefore

    b_epsilon,K_j(p,y_j)->b_epsilon,K(p,y).                     (5)

Maxima are attained since each of finitely many compact fibers has a
continuous depth function by the same argument. Choose converging
maximizers for the upper limit of the maxima; approximate a limit
maximizer by points of its corresponding approximating fiber for the
lower limit. Equation (5), and M_j->M>0, prove

    beta_epsilon(K_j)->beta_epsilon(K).                        (6)

The same proof is joint in epsilon_j->epsilon. In particular there is
no directionwise-only convergence or exchange of an uncontrolled
halfspace infimum and a limit.

On A, M=1, f<=1, and G_K(u)<=R for ||u||=1, since variance is no larger
than the second moment in the ball R B_d. Let

    L=m kappa_(d-1) R^(d-1).

The slab argument yields the useful uniform bound

    0<=b_epsilon,K(w)-b_0,K(w)<=epsilon L R,
    0<=beta_epsilon(K)-beta_0(K)<=epsilon L R.                  (7)

## 5. Attainment for all sufficiently small epsilon

Normalize the reference family into A. Choose epsilon_0>0 so small
that

    epsilon_0 L R < b-beta_0(K^ref).                           (8)

For 0<=epsilon<=epsilon_0, with a strict version of (8) at the endpoint,
let

    beta_epsilon^*=inf_K beta_epsilon(K),

where the infimum is over ALL positive compatible families on P.
The reference estimate (7) gives beta_epsilon^*<b. A late minimizing
sequence has beta_epsilon<=b and hence beta_0<=b. Normalize its total
mass to one and then apply the transformations in Section 2. By
Section 3, these do not change the buffered objective. The normalized
sequence lies in compact A. Equation (6) shows its limit attains
beta_epsilon^*, still with all fibers positive. Thus this is a genuine
unrestricted shape minimum, not merely a constrained normal-form
minimum.

The same argument at epsilon=0 recovers attainment of the original
infimum beta_0^*. Testing an original minimizer and using (7) gives

    beta_0^*<=beta_epsilon^*<=beta_0^*+epsilon L R.               (9)

Every sequence of these attained minima with epsilon decreasing to
zero has normalized subsequences in A whose limits attain beta_0^*.
This tracks the actual fibers, measures, candidate points and every
closed oblique halfspace; it changes no integer labels during the
limit on the fixed chosen base.

## 6. Uniform proper shifted own traces

There is one smaller positive epsilon_0 for which every buffered
maximizer at EVERY K in A has a proper own shifted trace in every
nonvertical direction. This is necessary for the finite critical-cap
and quantile arguments; pointwise smallness at the initial reference
family would not suffice.

Set c=gamma_d/m>0. Some fiber has volume at least 1/m. At its ordinary
centroid the continuous Gruenbaum inequality gives raw original depth
at least c, and therefore maximal buffered depth at least c. By (7),
a buffered maximizer w=(p,y) has

    b_0,K(p,y)>=c-epsilon L R.                                 (10)

Original depth is L-Lipschitz within each fiber and zero on its
boundary. The latter fact uses the canonical finite support roof: a
supporting covector of K_p at a boundary mark extends to a finite
ambient supporting covector of the compatible hull, so its outward
closed cap has zero volume in every positive d-dimensional fiber.
Equivalently solve the finite support-height linear program; the
proper-fiber support is tight at p and the attained dual roof bounds
all other fiber supports. Its continuous normal is nonzero, so closed
boundary traces have zero d-volume. Hence

    dist(y,boundary K_p)>=(c-epsilon L R)/L.                    (11)

Choose epsilon_0 L R<c/4. Then this distance is at least 3c/(4L), while
the displacement of the buffered own hyperplane is at most

    epsilon f_K(p,y)G_K(u)/||u||<=epsilon R<c/(4L).

The hyperplane therefore cuts the interior of K_p and leaves positive
volume on both sides. The source is interior uniformly in the entire
normalized compact sublevel class, not just at a fixed body.

## 7. What the theorem does and does not close

Under the original minimal-bad-base hypothesis, the invariant buffered
problem has an attained positive minimum for every sufficiently small
positive epsilon. Its deepest marks satisfy the precise smallness
condition needed by the proved finite critical-menu, full-supergradient,
fixed-parity-face cover and contact-minimum continuation theorems.
All compactification maps preserve the buffered normalized depth.

It follows that the invariant continuation theorem may legitimately
be applied at such a minimum: every actual nearby compatible path is
an admissible competitor. A proposed collection of response inequalities
that strictly lowers all covering masses would contradict minimality.

This does NOT prove that such a path exists. Regular-cap differentiation
still needs its stated regular trace hypotheses; supporting positive-area
facets require a separate coupled response. Neither uniform compactness
nor the positive contact credit supplies the factor gamma_d/k.
The sharp payment/obstruction theorem remains unproved.
